text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zambia Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) has welcomed the government's decision to do away with donor dependance, but said the sacrifice should not be carried only by workers but also by political leaders.
- The Zambia Independent Media Association said a media council to regulate journalists should not be run by the government, as proposed by President Frederick Chiluba, but by media practitioners.

- The opposition Zambia Democratic Congress has urged Zambia, which will host the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) heads of states summit in March, to facilitate a resolution on problems facing the trade group.
- Minister Without Portfolio Micheal Sata has denied he wants to replace President Frederick Chiluba when his second and last term ends in 2001.
- National Congress party chief Humphrey Muelemba was involved in a car crash last week while driving from a resort in Southern Zambia, police said.
